14% of the students from

students,

32 common plants of their country.

and
AIs because I can travel the world, I can recognize,

it's also making us very dependent from technology.

university courses? During the TETRIS project, we
identified that actually the subjects are
still often there, but they are hidden somewhere, and they
have disappeared from the titles and even the description of the
courses. Because what I said in the beginning, they sort of have
this feeling
that the students are a bit scared when they read these
terms and then would choose other courses, especially if they are
optional courses.
So
we want also to bring this back, and we hope
that taxonomy courses can dare to have them again
in universities

optional activities. Sometimes you

So during TETRIS, we created a MoU that
six partners signed to really agree to
work together on fostering taxonomic and
biodiversity information trainings, both in
academic trainings at universities, but also
in non-academic trainings and capacity building.

the next project that is called TETRIXX for TETRIS Next Level
that started this September and will go until 2030.

European certification system for taxonomic training,
pilots for taxonomic for the future initiative,

tools and AI.

spectrum, from field work to species classification.

funding bodies and the governments also support us more.
Now, what about biodiversity informatics?
Here we notice that there is a real risk of knowledge
transfer. As we know, TDWG exists since the mid-'80s.
As you saw, GBIF is celebrating its 25 years.
Yet, if you look it up, biodiversity informatics
is very rarely a topic or a master
in universities. As a striking example was the
master that was given at the Sorbonne University

by Régine Vigne, who gave presentations in the previous
sessions. And also Eli Saliba here in the room was part

another job, this course disappeared and is not continued,
which is really sad.
And also we identified that many
experts in the domain have a diploma of biologist of
bioengineers, but they specialized on the job and
they got passionate about it. But very few had actually
really a formal training except from trainings and
workshop where they learned biodiversity by learning from the
community and by themselves.
So what about biodiversity informatics and molecular
bioinformation? So these two disciplines over the years came
much closer. When I started my career, I felt
really a mistrust even between these two communities
because some molecular biologists claimed,
and some do it still now but it's less, that they could
get rid completely of classical and morphologic taxonomy and
that
everything with genetics could replace and make it much
easier to identify species and that we won't
need people to make it a classical way.
And then for a long time when we were collaborating, it
was very much limited that we wanted the voucher
specimens in the museums being kept and
linked to
the data about the sequences that were in the molecular

specimens that can confirm the genetic
identification. And it was not always easy to convince
everyone to really keep the specimen and to
add this information, but that was done.
And now in the past few decades, especially with the development of
barcoding and especially eDNA for biomonitoring,
there are even now TDWG standards on eDNA and
biogenomics and things have become much better
between the two communities and we have genuine very good
collaborations and standards and also joint trainings.

inventory of AI courses out there, and
we found out that many university, much faster than in our
domain, are now
setting up in a few years masters in AI.
They are popping up everywhere in all universities.

how AI has become important for our disciplines, this is
certainly a door for us to also get into this
university curricula and also get more funding,
by putting forwards our AI capacities.

important for the part on making the data AI-ready
because they need to be in a certain formal standard.
And we can also use AI to maybe generate
the data directly in TDWG standards, which should also
be quite interesting matter for this biodiversity
information modern curricula.
